observation_summary: The toDouble() method in the Dfp class incorrectly returned -Infinity instead of 0.0 when the Dfp value was zero, due to missing logic to handle the sign of zero.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding a conditional check (if (cmp0 == 0)) at the beginning of the toDouble() method to explicitly handle the zero case and return the correctly signed zero. This is a classic missing guard/validation check for a specific boundary condition (zero), which falls under the Checking category.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'May be the simplest way to fix it is to test the zero equality at the begin of the toDouble() method'
The fix_diff_oracle shows the addition of an 'if (cmp0 == 0)' check to handle the zero case before proceeding with other logic.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves returning a value, the root cause is the absence of a conditional check to distinguish zero from other values, not an incorrect initialization of a variable.
The fix is not a rewrite of the core algorithm, but rather the addition of a guard clause to handle a specific edge case (zero) that was previously falling through to incorrect logic.
